text.p: Dollar/mark's powerful correction was overdue and has plenty of scope to run further, after the 1.86 and 1.85 props gave way Friday, chartists said.
In coming sessions the decline could extend to 1.8265/85 marks, last week's lows, or even the first big retracement target just under 1.81, before the dollar finds its footing.

"It's a healthy correction of an extreme condition and I'd be looking for that 1.81 mark area to hold the decline," said Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston Corp.
The 38-percent retracment of the advance from May's 1.6680 mark low to Wednesday's eight-year high at 1.8913 lies near 1.8070, marking the first significant medium-term support, Spain said.
Since June, the upmove gathered speed at such a rate as to define a nearly parabolic trendline, experts said.
Before Friday, dollar/mark's rally had experienced only shallow corrections which nibbled away at overbought conditions. But now the daily RSI has moved back into more neutral territory.
"Its just very indicative of the market having lost an extremely powerful momentum structure that's been in place since June," said Rob Kepler, technical analyst at Lehman Brothers.
"I think it's pretty consistent with a correction idea, if the momemtum numbers go back to neutral zones and try to stabilize," he added.
Kepler said the break below the July 28 high at 1.8490 ultimately points to a test of the late July chart lows at 1.8265 and 1.8285.
In dollar/yen, meanwhile, the drop below chart support at 117 and 116.40 on Friday points to 114.00, the 62-percent retrace of the rally from 110.62 on June 11 to 119.58 on Wednesday, analysts said.
If 114 yen breaks, an old falling resistance line should act as support at 113.25 on Friday and at 112.75 on Monday, Spain said.
At 1400 EDT on Friday, the dollar was quoted at 1.8462/72 marks, down from 1.8600/05 at the open and at 114.55/65 yen, down from 117.22/27.
